description: Management portal: create static/management.html — a self-contained single-page app with purple/indigo dark theme, 5-section sidebar navigation. Depends on FEAT-001 (all management API endpoints must exist). Independent of FEAT-002 (customer portal).
steps: Step 1 — Create static/management.html as a single self-contained HTML file. Reuse the same CSS design language as static/index.html (purple/indigo theme, same CSS variable names: --bg, --surface, --indigo, --violet etc.) since they share the same design. Add management-specific accents. No external dependencies except Google Fonts Inter.

Step 2 — Login screen. ShopIQ Intelligence Platform branding. Username/password form. Demo hint box showing: admin/admin123, manager1/manager123. On submit: POST /auth/login; if role != 'manager' show error 'Access restricted to management accounts'; if success proceed to main app. On page load call GET /auth/me — if logged in as manager, skip login screen.

Step 3 — App shell: fixed left sidebar (240px) with logo (brain/shield icon), welcome message, 5 nav items: Dashboard (📊), Complaints (📋), Manage Complaint (🔧), Analytics (📈), Alerts (🚨). Top header bar: app name, logged-in user name, Logout button. Main content area right of sidebar. Page switching via JS show/hide sections.

Step 4 — Dashboard section. On load: call GET /api/complaints/summary for stats; call GET /api/complaints/alerts for early-warning banner. Render: 4 stat cards (Total, Critical, Negative, Avg Score — matching index.html pattern), Category bar chart (horizontal bars, same pattern as index.html using inline SVG-free approach), Sentiment donut chart (pure SVG, same as index.html), Priority bar chart. Early-warning alert banner: if alerts returned show a red/orange banner at top listing volume spikes and cluster alerts; if no alerts show a green 'All systems normal' notice.

Step 5 — Complaints section. Call GET /api/complaints on load/filter change. Filter dropdowns: Category, Sentiment, Priority, Status (new: open/in_progress/resolved/closed). Full table: ID, Customer, Channel, Category, Sentiment, Priority, Score bar, Status badge, Date, Manage button. Clicking Manage button stores complaint ID and switches to Manage Complaint section.

Step 6 — Manage Complaint section. Loaded when Manage button clicked from Complaints table. Call GET /api/complaints/<id>/detail. Layout: two-column upper (complaint info left, AI analysis right). Complaint info: text, metadata (date, channel, order/product). AI analysis card: category, sentiment, score bar, then call GET /api/complaints/<id>/priority-explanation and render the human-readable explanation as a collapsible block. Similar complaints panel: call GET /api/complaints/<id>/similar and list top 5 with their priority badges and a link to manage each. Actions panel: (a) Status update — dropdown (open/in_progress/resolved/closed) + Update button → PATCH /api/complaints/<id>/status; (b) Respond to customer — textarea + Send Response button → POST /api/complaints/<id>/respond, label says 'Customer will see this response'; (c) Internal note — textarea + Add Note button → POST /api/complaints/<id>/note, label says 'Internal only — not visible to customer'. Existing responses list below actions: show all responses (both customer-visible and internal notes with a 'Private' label). Refresh detail after each action.

Step 7 — Analytics section. Charts from existing API: call GET /api/complaints/summary for category/sentiment/priority distributions (bar + donut charts). Trend subsection: call GET /api/complaints/trends and render two charts: (a) Complaints per day for last 14 days — horizontal bar chart or sparkline using pure SVG; (b) Complaints by category for last 7 days — stacked horizontal bars. Use the same bar-chart rendering pattern as index.html (no external chart library). Label axes clearly.

Step 8 — Alerts section. Call GET /api/complaints/alerts on load. Three subsections: (a) Volume Spikes — table of categories with recent vs prior week counts and a warning badge; (b) High-Risk Clusters — cards showing cluster label, avg priority score bar, complaint count; (c) Critical Recent Complaints — table of critical complaints from last 48h with Manage button linking to Manage Complaint section. Show last-refreshed timestamp and a Refresh button. If all arrays are empty show 'No active alerts — all metrics normal' success card.

Step 9 — Ensure the existing index.html (internal dashboard at /) still works without login by NOT adding login_required to the summary/clusters/priority routes — actually FEAT-001 Step 4 adds @manager_required to those. This would break index.html which has no auth. Resolution: add a special bypass flag in the routes — OR better, keep index.html as a public internal tool and add a separate set of public summary endpoints. Correct approach: in routes.py, do NOT add @login_required or @manager_required to the existing read-only GET routes (summary, clusters, priority, list_complaints, get_complaint). Only add @login_required to POST /api/complaints (submit). The new management-specific routes (alerts, trends, respond, note, status) get @manager_required. The detail and responses routes get @login_required with ownership check. This preserves index.html working without auth while adding security to the new portal routes. Update FEAT-001 Step 4 accordingly — remove the decorators from existing read-only GET routes, only guard POST submit and all new routes.
acceptance_criteria: GET http://127.0.0.1:5000/management returns 200 with HTML content
Logging in as admin/admin123 shows management dashboard with stat cards and charts populated
Early-warning alert banner appears (or shows 'all normal') without JS error
Complaints table loads with all 20+ complaints, filters work
Clicking Manage on a complaint loads full detail with AI analysis and priority explanation
Posting a response via the Respond form creates a visible response (also appears in customer portal)
Adding an internal note does NOT appear in the customer portal Track view
Status update changes complaint status and reflects immediately
Analytics section loads trend charts without errors
Alerts section loads and shows the three subsections
Logging in as alice/alice123 on /management shows 'Access restricted to management accounts'
index.html at / still loads and shows data without login (public internal tool)
verification: cd complaint-intelligence && python main.py — server starts
Login as admin/admin123 — dashboard loads with stats
Navigate all 5 sections — no JS console errors, all API calls return data
Open http://127.0.0.1:5000 — existing index.html still works without login
Open http://127.0.0.1:5000/customer — login as alice, submit complaint, track it; login as admin on management and verify the complaint appears with Respond action working
findings: GET /management returns 200 (verified). GET / returns 200 (index.html still public, unaffected). Charts rendered with pure inline HTML bar rows and inline SVG donut (same pattern as index.html — no external chart libraries). Alerts, trends, similar, priority-explanation, detail, respond, note, status PATCH all routed correctly. The /api/complaints endpoint does not support filtering by status server-side so status filtering is applied client-side in the complaints table. Responses list in the Manage section uses the detail endpoint which returns responses array; internal notes (is_visible_to_customer=false) are marked with a Private badge.
